Continuation completed conceptually across all eight selected chapters. No score, range, ranking, or anchor recommendation assigned.

The repository shell was unavailable due to a sandbox startup failure, so I could not persist files. The following append-only manifest entries should be applied by the parent process, continuing from `E040`.

### New evidence units

#### 1B

- **E041** — GAO found in May 2022 that no reviewed DoD component fully complied with selected cybersecurity requirements for controlled-unclassified-information systems; reported implementation exceeded 70% but remained below DoD’s 100% requirement. This is target-period cyber-governance risk evidence, not a nuclear incident or personal Biden finding. [GAO report](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-22-105259). Mappings: `1B.3`, `1B.7`, `1B.8`, `1B.9`, `1B.10`; `8B.5`, `8B.8`.

- **E042** — State Department officials stated in August 2022 that the administration sought to reduce strategic risks through crisis communication, information sharing, arms-control engagement, and continuation of New START. This establishes declared risk-reduction diplomacy during the period, not measured risk reduction. [State Department remarks](https://2021-2025.state.gov/remarks-at-the-high-level-briefing-on-u-s-nuclear-policy-at-the-tenth-review-conference-on-the-treaty-on-the-non-proliferation-of-nuclear-weapons/). Mappings: `1B.5`, `1B.6`, `1B.8`, `1B.10`; `2B.3`, `8B.2`, `8B.6`.

Shortfall remains: no public evidence establishes 2022 command-and-control performance, classified crisis decisions, or operational nuclear safety.

#### 2B

- **E043** — State and USAID inspectors general announced in August 2022 that Ukraine oversight was a priority and that their teams were conducting field visits, audit work, and fraud-risk reviews concerning humanitarian assistance. This documents oversight activation and accountability infrastructure, not proof of civilian-harm prevention or Biden responsibility. [OIG joint visit](https://www.stateoig.gov/investigative-press-release/oig-delegation-conducts-joint-visit-advance-ukraine-response-oversight). Mappings: `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.9`, `2B.10`; `8B.5`, `8B.8`, `8B.9`.

- **E044** — Contemporary reporting documented difficulty conducting in-person inspections of U.S.-provided weapons in Ukraine and the administration’s effort to strengthen tracking under battlefield conditions. This is contrary partner-control and accountability evidence; it does not establish diversion or unlawful conduct. [Washington Post report](https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2022/11/01/us-weapons-ukraine-oversight/). Mappings: `2B.5`, `2B.7`, `2B.9`, `2B.10`; `8B.5`, `8B.8`.

Shortfall remains: no independent 2022 finding connects a specific U.S. decision to civilian harm, proportionality failure, or partner misconduct.

#### 3B

- **E045** — DOJ opened a June 2022 pattern-or-practice investigation into the NYPD Special Victims Division, examining gender-biased policing, treatment of sexual-assault survivors, investigative procedures, staffing, and support services. This is federal enforcement activity addressing vulnerable-group protection, but it is an investigation rather than a completed outcome finding and concerns local conduct. [DOJ announcement](https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/justice-department-announces-investigation-new-york-city-police-department-s-special-victims). Mappings: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.4`, `3B.5`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `3B.10`; `8B.5`, `8B.8`.

Shortfall remains: no nationwide or state/local outcome measure permits broad Biden attribution.

#### 4B

- **E046** — The Committee to Protect Journalists’ January 2022 assessment described a substantial reversal from the prior administration’s hostile media rhetoric and a return toward more conventional White House–press relations, while noting that several press-freedom promises had not yet become action. This is mixed independent context, not proof of Biden’s personal treatment of dissent. [CPJ assessment](https://cpj.org/2022/01/report-on-press-freedom-finds-mix-of-problems-and-progress-under-biden-administration/). Mappings: `4B.3`, `4B.6`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`; `7B.8`, `8B.6`, `8B.8`.

- **E047** — The bipartisan Election Assistance Commission later published comprehensive administrative and voting data for the 2022 midterms. This provides an observable election-administration record, but the commission is independent and state/local administration remains outside direct presidential control. [EAC report announcement](https://www.eac.gov/news/2023/06/29/nations-most-comprehensive-report-2022-midterm-election-administration-and-voting). Mappings: `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.4`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`; `8B.5`, `8B.8`.

Shortfall remains: Biden-specific evidence concerning surveillance practice, appointments, retaliation, and practical political equality is thin.

#### 5B

- **E048** — CBO estimated that Biden’s August 2022 student-loan actions increased federal student-loan costs by approximately $400 billion in present value, including about $20 billion from the temporary payment suspension and roughly $400 billion from debt cancellation. This is realized policy-cost evidence with clear executive attribution, but its broader fiscal and distributional effects remain contested. [CBO estimate](https://www.cbo.gov/publication/58494). Mappings: `5B.3`, `5B.6`, `5B.7`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`; `8B.1`, `8B.2`, `8B.6`, `8B.7`.

Shortfall remains: implementation quality, employment/productivity effects, inflation causation, and policy correction remain unresolved.

#### 6B

- **E049** — GAO reported in March 2022 that insured consumers faced difficulty finding in-network mental-health providers, with stakeholders identifying reimbursement and network-adequacy problems. This is contemporaneous general-population access evidence, but it is not a Biden-specific outcome finding. [GAO mental-health access testimony](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-22-105912). Mappings: `6B.1`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`, `6B.6`, `6B.8`, `6B.10`; `8B.5`, `8B.8`.

- **E050** — GAO found that VA did not centrally track or adequately oversee its nongovernmental mental-health and suicide-prevention partnerships, despite their intended role in expanding veteran access. This is adverse implementation evidence within the period, not a personal Biden finding. [GAO report](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-22-104674). Mappings: `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`, `6B.6`, `6B.9`, `6B.10`; `8B.5`, `8B.8`.

Shortfall remains: service quality, affordability, regional equity, and durable general-population outcomes are not established.

#### 7B

No new defensible Biden-specific personal-integrity evidence was recovered.

The targeted contrary search found later congressional reports and partisan allegations concerning Hunter Biden, censorship, and DOJ processes, but these were either post-period, contested, not independently corroborated, or failed to establish a personal 2022 finding against Joe Biden. They should remain rejected and should not receive provisional evidence IDs.

The chapter remains materially underdetermined on enrichment, deception, obstruction, nepotism, retaliation, and independently adjudicated personal findings.

#### 8B

- **E051** — EAC’s 2022 midterm dataset supplies an observable administrative record for election operations, while also illustrating the limits of presidential attribution because election administration is distributed across state and local systems and the independent EAC. [EAC announcement](https://www.eac.gov/news/2023/06/29/nations-most-comprehensive-report-2022-midterm-election-administration-and-voting). Mappings: `8B.1`, `8B.2`, `8B.5`, `8B.6`, `8B.8`, `8B.9`.

- **E052** — CBO’s student-loan estimate provides a clear, contemporaneous policy-output and fiscal-cost record, but not a durable welfare or effectiveness outcome. [CBO estimate](https://www.cbo.gov/publication/58494). Mappings: `8B.1`, `8B.2`, `8B.5`, `8B.6`, `8B.7`, `8B.8`.
